comment: ONLY files listed under 'migrations' with idempotent:true are auto-applied
at startup, in the order listed. A file may be listed ONLY if every one of
its statements is safe to re-run on every boot: CREATE TABLE/INDEX IF NOT
EXISTS, ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS, INSERT ... ON CONFLICT,
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION/VIEW, DROP-IF-EXISTS-then-CREATE trigger pairs,
COMMENT ON, GRANT, CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS. No DROPs of data, no
unguarded INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, no type changes. Files that fail the bar
stay in 'needs_review' (documentation only — the runner ignores it).

migrations.notes: app_model_lists / app_model_list_items / user_model_preferences / model_access_audit. All DDL is IF NOT EXISTS or OR REPLACE; triggers are DROP IF EXISTS + CREATE pairs; single seed INSERT is ON CONFLICT (slug) DO NOTHING. Ends with the 2026-07-02 convergence ALTER ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS block that model_list_manager.py depends on (is_active/is_featured/tier_*_access/metadata).

org_features table + indexes + org_has_feature() helper + v_org_features_with_names view. Fully re-runnable: CREATE EXTENSION/TABLE/INDEX IF NOT EXISTS, CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION/VIEW, COMMENT ON, GRANT, DO-block that only RAISEs NOTICEs; the sample INSERT is commented out. FK depends on organizations(id uuid) — created earlier in startup by migrations/core, and a non-benign failure just retries next boot.

needs_review.reason: NOT auto-applied. (1) usage_alerts DDL is invalid PostgreSQL — 'CONSTRAINT unique_user_alert UNIQUE(user_id, alert_type, created_at::DATE)' puts an expression in a table UNIQUE constraint (needs a CREATE UNIQUE INDEX instead), so the CREATE TABLE fails every run and the table can never converge from this file. (2) It installs AFTER INSERT/UPDATE triggers that mutate usage_quotas on the api_usage hot write path plus a 90-day MATERIALIZED VIEW — runtime behavior changes, not just schema convergence. Fix the DDL and decide on the triggers before listing.
